production.note: US model years 2021 to 2025. Stuttcars: "Model Years: 2021 - 2025" and "sold through 2025 before the hybridized 992.2 arrived". First: pcna-2021-turbo-s-press-kit and the spec sheet porsche-2021-turbo-s-us-specs name the launch car the "2021 911 Turbo S" ("expected to reach U.S. dealers in late 2020"). Last: pcna-2024-turbo-50-years refers to "the current 2025 911 Turbo S (992.1)".

body.note: Spec sheet columns: "2021 911 Turbo S" and "2021 911 Turbo S Cabriolet". The Cabriolet is the open version of the same variant, so it is listed here rather than as its own record.

configuration.note: Spec sheet: engine type "Boxer, twin-turbo", 6 cylinders

displacementL.note: 3,745 cc. Spec sheet: "3.745 l", rounded to 3.7. Porsche's launch press kit pcna-2021-turbo-s-press-kit marketed it as a "3.8 liter boxer engine"; pcna-2024-turbo-50-years says "3.7 liter". See discrepancies.

aspiration.note: Spec sheet: "Boxer, twin-turbo". Press kit: "Two VTG turbochargers".

drivetrain.note: Spec sheet: "Active all-wheel drive" (Porsche Traction Management)

transmission.note: Spec sheet: "8-speed dual-clutch PDK". DCT is Porsche PDK; no manual was offered (stuttcars-992-turbo-s: "8-speed PDK dual-clutch only (no manual on Turbo S)").

powerHp.note: Quote: "Maximum Power Output: 640 hp @ 6,750" (Coupe and Cabriolet columns). Corroborated by pcna-2021-turbo-s-press-kit: "The most powerful six-cylinder boxer engine currently offered by Porsche now delivers 640 hp, 60 hp more than its predecessor." The rating was still 640 hp for 2025 (pcna-2024-turbo-50-years).

weightLb.note: Coupe with the standard 8-speed PDK and standard equipment. Quote: "Curb Weight: 3636 lbs. | 3790 lbs." under the columns "2021 911 Turbo S | 2021 911 Turbo S Cabriolet". The Cabriolet is 3,790 lb. The optional Lightweight Package (about 66 lb lighter per the press kit) is not included.

discrepancies.reason: Same engine, described two ways by Porsche. The exact figure in the US spec sheet is 3.745 l (3,745 cc). The 2020 launch press kit markets it as a "3.8 liter" engine; Porsche's 2024 release for the 2025 model year calls it "3.7 liter".
discrepancies.resolution: 3.7 used: the guide says to use the cc figure rounded to one decimal of a litre, whatever the marketing says.

discrepancies.reason: Stuttcars prints both "640 bhp @ 6750 rpm" and "641 hp @ 6750 rpm". 641 hp is the conversion of the European 650 PS rating; 640 hp is Porsche's published US rating.
discrepancies.resolution: 640 used: the manufacturer's US rating as published, per the guide.
